reducer_input_inertia.evidence: blank; counted as zero only in the workbook-equivalent model, not measured zero

kt_output.evidence: test value at the actuator output

brake_multiplier.evidence: estimated ten-percent difference, not an independent braking test

corner_rpm.evidence: rated-current speed; the worksheet warns the speed falls at the current limit

figure_definitions.Y1: peak torque with torque and speed in the same direction
figure_definitions.Y2: peak torque with torque and speed in opposite directions
figure_definitions.X1: maximum speed at full torque, idealized knee point
figure_definitions.Va: velocity at which friction is fully activated; not a speed limit

friction_activation_rpm.context: output unloaded, VESC no-load test; not the T-N endpoint

metadata.excluded_profile: The attachment-2 ADAM Lite PNDrive current-to-torque scale belongs to a separate configuration and is not mixed into this profile.

modeling_caveats: The user selected this row and its embedded directional envelope as the simulation source of truth.

The output-equivalent inertia is derived once from input-side inertia and gear ratio. The MuJoCo coordinate is already the gearbox-output/crank angle: use transmission gear 1, not another factor of the physical gear ratio.

The default inertia policy includes existing explicit moving-body axial inertia in the output-shaft budget. Subtracting it to allocate armature is bookkeeping, not a measured hidden-rotor inertia. An external-extra policy must be selected explicitly.
The empty reducer inertia is unknown; treating its blank value as zero reproduces the supplied workbook, not a verified complete gearbox inertia.
The supplied knee is a rated-current speed. The idealized peak envelope is not a verified full-current torque-speed measurement at that knee.
Continuous mode means the rated-current torque cap intersected with the directional peak envelope. It is not a measured thermal capability curve or a guarantee of indefinite operation.
Braking capacity is an estimated output-torque envelope. Dividing every braking torque by the tested drive torque constant is not a validated phase-current model.
No friction, electrical, thermal, or regeneration dynamics are inferred from missing data. Friction-activation speed is metadata only.
Beyond the no-load speed, driving torque is zero and estimated braking remains available; this extrapolation is not an overspeed-safety guarantee. Velocity itself must not be clipped.
RPM is converted using exact 2*pi/60, not the worksheet's rounded 6.28/60 cached formulas.
